title: Asset size threshold and regulatory burden on bank profitability

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)
- Why: Treatment (additional regulation) turns on deterministically at the $10B asset threshold. Using the running variable (log assets normalized; cutoff = 0.5) allows identification from the discontinuity in ROA at the threshold, comparing banks just above vs. just below.
- Key assumptions:
  - Continuity: In the absence of treatment, the conditional expectation of ROA is continuous in assets at the cutoff.
  - No precise manipulation: Banks cannot perfectly sort just above/below the cutoff in a way correlated with potential outcomes. Given concerns about strategic size management, we will:
    - Test for bunching near the cutoff (simple density/balance test).
    - Use a donut-RD (exclude the closest observations) to mitigate manipulation right at the threshold.
    - Provide a local-randomization estimate within a narrow window as a robustness check.
  - Stable relationship locally: A local linear approximation of the outcome-running variable relationship is appropriate near the cutoff.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code for RDD analysis on the provided dataset

# 0) Setup -------------------------------------------------------------------
suppressWarnings({
  if (!requireNamespace("sandwich", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("sandwich")
  if (!requireNamespace("lmtest", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("lmtest")
})
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

options(scipen = 9, digits = 4)

# 1) Load data ---------------------------------------------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s28_data.csv"
dat <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(dat) <- trimws(names(dat))

# Basic checks and cleaning
stopifnot(all(c("running_var","treated","y","near_cutoff") %in% names(dat)))
dat <- subset(dat, is.finite(running_var) & is.finite(treated) & is.finite(y) & is.finite(near_cutoff))

# 2) Design parameters -------------------------------------------------------
c0 <- 0.5  # cutoff in normalized units
x  <- dat$running_var
y  <- dat$y
D_given <- as.integer(dat$treated)
near_flag <- as.integer(dat$near_cutoff)

# Sanity check: does treated == 1[x >= c0]?
D_by_x <- as.integer(x >= c0)
mismatch <- sum(D_by_x != D_given, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("Sanity check: mismatches between treated and 1[x>=cutoff] =", mismatch, "out of", nrow(dat), "\n")

# 3) Helper: local linear RD with triangular kernel --------------------------
local_linear_rd <- function(y, x, c, h, data_subset = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(data_subset)) {
    y <- y[data_subset]; x <- x[data_subset]
  }
  R <- x - c
  keep <- abs(R) <= h
  y <- y[keep]; x <- x[keep]; R <- R[keep]
  D <- as.integer(x >= c)
  # Triangular kernel weights
  w <- pmax(0, 1 - abs(R)/h)
  # Fit: y ~ D + R + D:R, weighted local linear
  fit <- lm(y ~ D * R, weights = w)
  # Robust (HC1) SE
  vc <- tryCatch(vcovHC(fit, type = "HC1"), error = function(e) vcov(fit))
  coefs <- coef(fit)
  se <- sqrt(diag(vc))
  if (!("D" %in% names(coefs))) {
    return(list(tau = NA, se = NA, n = length(y), h = h))
  }
  tau <- unname(coefs["D"])
  se_tau <- unname(se["D"])
  tval <- tau / se_tau
  pval <- 2 * pt(abs(tval), df = max(1, length(y) - length(coefs)), lower.tail = FALSE)
  ci_low <- tau - 1.96 * se_tau
  ci_high <- tau + 1.96 * se_tau
  return(list(tau = tau, se = se_tau, pval = pval, ci = c(ci_low, ci_high), n = length(y), h = h))
}

# Choose a practical baseline bandwidth ensuring enough data per side
# Start with h0 = 0.2, expand if too few obs on one side (<30) within window
choose_bandwidth <- function(x, c, start = 0.2, step = 0.05, max_h = 0.6, min_per_side = 30) {
  h <- start
  while (h <= max_h) {
    idx <- abs(x - c) <= h
    left <- sum(x[idx] < c)
    right <- sum(x[idx] >= c)
    if (left >= min_per_side && right >= min_per_side) return(h)
    h <- h + step
  }
  return(min(max_h, h)) # return largest tried if constraint not met
}
h0 <- choose_bandwidth(x, c0, start = 0.2, step = 0.05, max_h = 0.6, min_per_side = 30)

# 4) Manipulation/bunching check near cutoff --------------------------------
# Simple bin test: compare counts just right vs just left within a very narrow window
w_b <- 0.05
near_idx <- abs(x - c0) <= w_b
left_cnt <- sum(x[near_idx] < c0)
right_cnt <- sum(x[near_idx] >= c0)
total_cnt <- left_cnt + right_cnt
log_ratio <- ifelse(min(left_cnt, right_cnt) > 0, log((right_cnt) / (left_cnt)), NA)
p_bunch <- if (total_cnt > 0) binom.test(right_cnt, total_cnt, p = 0.5, alternative = "two.sided")$p.value else NA

cat("\nBunching check within +/-", w_b, "of cutoff:\n")
cat(" Left count =", left_cnt, " Right count =", right_cnt, " Total =", total_cnt, "\n")
cat(" Log(right/left) =", round(log_ratio, 4), "  Binomial p-value =", signif(p_bunch, 4), "\n")

# 5) Baseline sharp RD (local linear, triangular kernel) ---------------------
rd_baseline <- local_linear_rd(y, x, c = c0, h = h0, data_subset = NULL)
cat("\nBaseline local-linear RD (triangular kernel):\n")
cat(" Bandwidth h =", rd_baseline$h, "  N used =", rd_baseline$n, "\n")
cat(" RD estimate (jump in ROA at cutoff) =", round(rd_baseline$tau, 6),
    " SE =", round(rd_baseline$se, 6),
    "  95% CI [", round(rd_baseline$ci[1], 6), ",", round(rd_baseline$ci[2], 6), "]",
    "  p-value =", signif(rd_baseline$pval, 4), "\n")

# 6) Donut RD: exclude observations flagged as 'near_cutoff' -----------------
donut_idx <- (near_flag == 0)
rd_donut <- local_linear_rd(y, x, c = c0, h = h0, data_subset = donut_idx)
cat("\nDonut RD (exclude near_cutoff==1):\n")
cat(" Bandwidth h =", rd_donut$h, "  N used =", rd_donut$n, "\n")
cat(" RD estimate =", round(rd_donut$tau, 6),
    " SE =", round(rd_donut$se, 6),
    "  95% CI [", round(rd_donut$ci[1], 6), ",", round(rd_donut$ci[2], 6), "]",
    "  p-value =", signif(rd_donut$pval, 4), "\n")

# 7) Local-randomization estimate within near window -------------------------
# Use near_cutoff==1 window as-if randomized: difference in means
lr_idx <- (near_flag == 1)
if (sum(lr_idx & (x < c0)) > 5 && sum(lr_idx & (x >= c0)) > 5) {
  y_left <- y[lr_idx & (x < c0)]
  y_right <- y[lr_idx & (x >= c0)]
  diff_lr <- mean(y_right) - mean(y_left)
  tt <- t.test(y_right, y_left, var.equal = FALSE)
  cat("\nLocal-randomization (within near_cutoff==1) difference-in-means:\n")
  cat(" N_left =", length(y_left), " N_right =", length(y_right), "\n")
  cat(" Diff (ROA|right - ROA|left) =", round(diff_lr, 6),
      "  95% CI [", round(tt$conf.int[1], 6), ",", round(tt$conf.int[2], 6), "]",
      "  p-value =", signif(tt$p.value, 4), "\n")
} else {
  cat("\nLocal-randomization: insufficient data on one side within near_cutoff==1 window.\n")
}

# 8) Global polynomial RD (cubic) as robustness ------------------------------
R <- x - c0
D <- as.integer(x >= c0)
poly_df <- data.frame(y = y, D = D, R = R)
gfit <- lm(y ~ D * poly(R, 3, raw = TRUE), data = poly_df)
gvc <- tryCatch(vcovHC(gfit, type = "HC1"), error = function(e) vcov(gfit))
gcoefs <- coef(gfit)
gse <- sqrt(diag(gvc))
tau_g <- unname(gcoefs["D"])
se_g  <- unname(gse["D"])
t_g   <- tau_g / se_g
p_g   <- 2 * pt(abs(t_g), df = max(1, nrow(poly_df) - length(gcoefs)), lower.tail = FALSE)
ci_g  <- c(tau_g - 1.96 * se_g, tau_g + 1.96 * se_g)

cat("\nGlobal polynomial RD (cubic):\n")
cat(" RD estimate =", round(tau_g, 6),
    " SE =", round(se_g, 6),
    "  95% CI [", round(ci_g[1], 6), ",", round(ci_g[2], 6), "]",
    "  p-value =", signif(p_g, 4), "\n")

# 9) Brief summary line ------------------------------------------------------
cat("\nSummary (baseline RD): point estimate =", round(rd_baseline$tau, 6),
    ", p-value =", signif(rd_baseline$pval, 4),
    "; Donut RD:", round(rd_donut$tau, 6), ", p-value =", signif(rd_donut$pval, 4), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Crossing the $10B threshold should reduce ROA due to higher compliance and supervisory costs and potential operational frictions.
- Magnitude: Economically modest but nontrivial locally at the cutoff. I expect a small decline in ROA—on the order of a few to several basis points relative to typical bank ROA—roughly a negative jump that is small relative to the cross-sectional standard deviation (e.g., −0.05 to −0.15 standard deviations). The donut and local-randomization estimates should be similar in sign and slightly smaller in magnitude if manipulation right at the cutoff biases the naive estimate.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Sharp RDD — asset threshold; test for bunching below $10B; local linear regression
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Banks just above threshold have lower ROA than just-below peers
